snapshots.projNote: Strength is ESPN’s own projection for each week (weeks 1 to 14), with the best legal lineup filled rather than the one currently set (9 starters read from the current lineups) — the same total the ESPN site shows under a lineup paged forward to that week, except that a bench player projected above a starter is counted as starting. Players on bye come back at zero from ESPN, so they sit down on their own.

snapshots.projNote: Strength is ESPN’s own projection for each week (weeks 4 to 14), with the best legal lineup filled rather than the one currently set (9 starters read from the current lineups) — the same total the ESPN site shows under a lineup paged forward to that week, except that a bench player projected above a starter is counted as starting. A player on bye projects zero, so the best lineup starts someone else where it can; a slot still worth less than the waiver wire would give you at that position is counted at the wire’s figure instead (the positional floor). The playoff weeks (15, 16, 17) are read the same way and used only by the simulation below — the regular season ends at week 14 and the bracket has no games until it is seeded, so those weeks are asked for by number.
